reason: Part b is well shown by a family of solution curves through (1, 1), where the slider k is tuned until the curve hits (25, 3). Part a is symbol manipulation, so it gets no scene.

scenes.title: Tuning k so the solution curve passes through both points
scenes.purpose: See that the condition (1, 1) fixes the constant c, and the condition (25, 3) then picks out the single value of k.

steps.text: With $x=1$ and $y=1$ we get $\ln\left(\frac15\right)=6k\ln 1+c$, so $c=-\ln 5$ whatever $k$ is. Drag $k$: every curve passes through $(1,1)$. This is the B1 for finding $c$ first.

The second point $(25,3)$ makes the left side $\ln 1=0$, giving $0=6k\ln 25-\ln 5$. On the board, the curve only passes through $(25,3)$ for one value of $k$. This is the M1 for an equation in $k$ alone.
Use $\ln 25=2\ln 5$ to get $12k\ln 5=\ln 5$, so $k=\frac1{12}\approx 0.0833$. Set $k$ to this value and the curve hits $(25,3)$. These are the M1 and A1 for solving for $k$.

With $6k=\frac12$, $\frac{y}{6-y}=\frac{\sqrt x}{5}$ rearranges to $y=\frac{6\sqrt x}{5+\sqrt x}$. This is the curve drawn, so $A=6$, $B=5$, $n=\frac12$. Drag $G$ along it: $y$ stays below $6$. These are the last M1 and A1.

interact.do: Drag the slider between $0.02$ and $0.2$, then set it to about $0.0833$ (that is $\frac{1}{12}$).
interact.watch: Every curve passes through $(1,1)$, but the height at $x=25$ changes. The curve passes through $(25,3)$ only when $k=\frac{1}{12}\approx 0.0833$, where $6k=0.5$ and the readout shows $3$.

interact.do: Drag $G$ along the curve from near $x=0$ out to $x=40$.
interact.watch: With $k=\frac{1}{12}$, $G$ passes through $(1,1)$ and $(25,3)$. Its height keeps rising but stays below the line $y=6$, which fits $0<y<6$.

legend.meaning: The solution curve $y=\dfrac{6x^{6k}}{5+x^{6k}}$ for the current $k$. It already satisfies $y=1$ at $x=1$ (so $c=-\ln 5$).
The given point $(1,1)$. It fixes $c=-\ln 5$, whatever $k$ is.
The given point $(25,3)$. It fixes the value of $k$.
A point you can drag along the solution curve $S$ to read off its position.
The horizontal line $y=6$, which the solution never reaches.
The vertical line $x=25$, where the curve must have height $3$.

question_link.text: The curve $S$ is the solution $y$ of the differential equation, and $P1$ and $P2$ are the two given conditions. Every curve passing through $P1$ shows the B1 for $c=-\ln 5$. Needing $S$ to hit $P2$ is the M1 equation in $k$, and $k=\frac{1}{12}$ is the A1. The curve then matches $y=\frac{6\sqrt{x}}{5+\sqrt{x}}$, so $A=6$, $B=5$, $n=\frac12$.

read_off: The 'readout' label gives the height of the curve at $x=25$, which is $\frac{6\cdot 25^{6k}}{5+25^{6k}}$. It must equal $3$ for the curve to pass through $(25,3)$, and it does so when $k=\frac{1}{12}$.
The '$6k$' label gives the index $n$ in $y=\frac{6x^{n}}{5+x^{n}}$. At $k=\frac{1}{12}$ it reads about $0.5$, so $n=\frac12$.
guide.what_you_see: The solution curve $S$ of $x\\frac{\\mathrm{d}y}{\\mathrm{d}x}=ky(6-y)$, drawn as $y=\\frac{6x^{6k}}{5+x^{6k}}$, with the given points $(1,1)$ and $(25,3)$ and the ceiling $y=6$. The slider $k$ changes the curve.
